data.narrative:
Rigetti Computing is a public-stage quantum computing company currently valued at $4.5B. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of four same-sector, same-stage companies: IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), Infleqtion ($1.9B), and Archer Materials ($60M). The quantum computing sector includes three public comps (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and eight additional private peers.

The peer-median method, the primary applicable triangulation approach given single-method constraints, yields an implied valuation of $4.1B across the four-company cohort. This method reflects substantial dispersion in the comp universe, with valuations ranging from $60M to $13.0B—a 216x spread that reflects heterogeneity in development stage, technical approach, and commercialization progress within quantum computing. The peer median of $4.1B sits approximately 9% below Rigetti's current mark of $4.5B.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $3.5B to $4.7B (median $4.1B), centered on peer comparables. Primary uncertainties stem from the wide valuation dispersion across comps and the nascent, pre-revenue or early-revenue profile of most quantum computing platforms. The current $4.5B valuation sits within the implied range and proximate to the peer median, though the extreme outliers in the comp set (IonQ at $13.0B; Archer Materials at $60M) underscore material disagreement in market pricing of quantum development trajectories. Additional capital raises, technical milestones, and commercial traction would be required to narrow valuation confidence intervals.
